messages:
Marta Ruiz: Quick check: compact Console form final decisions. Two axes: required-field signal (asterisk vs explicit small "Required") and validation surface (compact inline vs top-level toast summary). Constraints: dense rows, many accordions, keyboard-first.
Devin Chen: Inline mapping is best UX-wise but causes layout shift in dense layout. Lean toast summary + lightweight inline marker.
Ellie Wong: Accessibility: if markers are visual-only we must expose programmatic cues. Always set aria-invalid on invalid inputs and aria-describedby pointing to the error message (even if visually hidden).
Jamal Patel: For collapsed sections: toast items should anchor to field IDs and open the parent accordion + focus the field. Avoid setTimeout hacks. Use role=alert on the error node when revealed.
Marta Ruiz: Required marker debate: asterisk is compact but ambiguous. Proposal: persistent tiny "Required" on first item in a group + global legend, or compact asterisk with high-contrast color + aria-label.
Devin Chen: If using asterisk, ensure WCAG contrast in dim theme and add data-required="true" for automation.
Ellie Wong: Destructive flows: typed-confirm only for irreversible data deletes (DB, audit logs). For single-item UI deletes use modal + undo toast. Token should be a single lowercase word (no punctuation). Show resource name+id.
Jamal Patel: Toast collisions: only one toast visible. Priority queue: error > undo > info. Queue lower-priority toasts.
Marta Ruiz: Action items: produce two mock variants: (A) toast summary w/ anchor links + compact inline markers + ARIA, (B) persistent tiny "Required" postfix + inline helpers. Include SR announce tests, keyboard-only flows, and focus behavior when opening accordions.
design-bot: Filed: https://go.redwood/design/issues/CI-572 "Dense forms: marker vs summary + a11y checklist". Assigned @Marta.
Devin Chen: CSS/QA nit: focus ring for compact inputs must be >=3px and meet contrast on dim theme.
Ellie Wong: +1. I'll draft a11y test cases.
Marta Ruiz: Thanks team. I'll post Figma mocks by EOD Thursday and a short test matrix.
